cards.en: nominative: the subject; the basic dictionary form
cards.hint: talo = the house (as the subject: Talo on iso = The house is big)

cards.en: genitive: possession ("of", 's); also the object of a verb (accusative)
cards.hint: talo → talon = the house's / of the house. Mikon auto = Mikko's car. Näen talon = I see the house

cards.en: partitive: "some" / part of something; used after numbers and in negatives
cards.hint: Juon kahvia = I drink (some) coffee. kaksi kahvia = two coffees. Ei ole kahvia = there is no coffee
talossa = in the house. Trick: the double s is for "inSide"
talosta = out of the house. Trick: -sta = "start out" from inside
talo → taloon = into the house (the last vowel doubles + n). Trick: ends in n like "in(to)"
pöydällä = on the table. Minulla on kirja = I have a book (literally, "at me is a book")

cards.en: ablative: from (a surface or a person)
cards.hint: pöydältä = from the table. Sain kirjeen Mikolta = I got a letter from Mikko
pöydälle = onto the table. Annan sen Mikolle = I give it to Mikko
opettajana = as a teacher. maanantaina = on Monday
Hän opiskelee opettajaksi = he/she is studying to become a teacher. Trick: -ksi = "ex-", changing into something
rahatta = without money. In everyday speech people use ilman + partitive instead: ilman maitoa = without milk
lapsineen = with his/her children. Set phrase more than everyday speech

cards.en: instructive: by means of, in the manner of (rare)
cards.hint: omin silmin = with my own eyes. Mostly in set phrases
talo → talot = the houses

cards.en: plural stem: more than one in the other cases
cards.hint: taloissa = in the houses (talo + i + ssa)
talojen = of the houses
taloja = (some) houses. Haluan omenoita = I want (some) apples
kirja → kirjani = my book
kirjasi = your book
kirjansa = his/her/their book
kirjamme = our book
kirjanne = y'all's book

cards.en: turns a statement into a yes/no question
cards.hint: Onko kahvia? = Is there coffee? (on + ko). Tuletko? = Are you coming?
Minäkin tulen = I'm coming too
Minäkään en tiedä = I don't know either
Sehän on selvää = well, that's obvious
Onpa kaunis päivä! = What a beautiful day!
iso → isompi = bigger
iso → isoin = biggest
